nc0856679dd9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the du-aspa sih-aspa arrangement?
o: It raised the zat rank of the mansabdar.
Part of the sawar rank was counted double.
nc0856679dd9.x: Du-aspa sih-aspa counted part of the sawar rank twice for trusted mansabdars without raising their zat.

nd81249528e8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Mughal central ministers?
o: Wazir or Diwan – finance and revenue
Mir Bakhshi – military pay, mansabs and intelligence
Mir Saman – religion, charity and madad-i-maash grants
Sadr-us-Sudur – religion, charity and madad-i-maash grants
nd81249528e8.x: The Mir Saman supervised the royal household and karkhanas; religion and charity were under the Sadr-us-Sudur.

n323c7b3b685.s: In the Mughal administrative hierarchy, the pargana stood immediately above the:
n323c7b3b685.x: The order from lowest to highest was village, pargana, sarkar and subah, so the pargana stood just above the village.

n6064bc5fc7c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the categories of zamindars in Mughal India?
o: Autonomous chiefs were Rajas ruling their own territories.
Primary zamindars held only temporary, non-hereditary rights over land.
Intermediary zamindars collected revenue from primary zamindars for a commission.
Autonomous chiefs paid tribute and served as mansabdars.
n6064bc5fc7c.x: Primary zamindars did not hold merely temporary, non-hereditary rights; the other three statements are correct.

nb9a4a6d8245.s: In Qutb Shahi Golconda, land revenue was mainly:
o: Assessed only through the Dahsala system
Collected by village panchayats without intermediaries
Assessed only through Kankut crop estimates
nb9a4a6d8245.x: Qutb Shahi Golconda farmed out its revenue by auction; the Northern Circars zamindars date from that era.

new.s: Aurangzeb was popularly called by which epithet for his simple, pious life?
new.x: He was popularly known as Zinda Pir ('Living Saint'); Alamgir was his regnal title.

new.s: Which royal woman received the title Padshah Begum under Aurangzeb?
new.x: Roshanara, who backed Aurangzeb in the succession war, was Padshah Begum; Jahanara was Sahibat-uz-Zamani.

new.s: In which year did Aurangzeb reimpose the jizya?
new.x: Jizya was reimposed in 1679, the year the Rajput war began; 1669 was the temple order.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Aurangzeb's religious measures:
1. He stopped jharokha darshan and tuladan.
2. He banned the Navroz celebration.
3. He abolished the jizya.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: He stopped jharokha darshan and tuladan and banned Navroz; he reimposed the jizya, which Akbar had abolished.

new.s: The state-made secular regulations issued under Aurangzeb were known as:
new.x: Zawabit were state-made secular regulations; Aurangzeb stressed the supremacy of Sharia over them.

new.s: According to Athar Ali, the share of Hindu nobles under Aurangzeb (1679–1707) rose to about:
new.x: Athar Ali shows the Hindu share in the nobility rose to about 31.6%, many of them Marathas.

new.s: Who championed the cause of Ajit Singh, the posthumous son of Jaswant Singh of Marwar?
new.x: Durgadas Rathore championed Ajit Singh; Rana Raj Singh of Mewar joined Marwar in the war.

new.s: The rebel Mughal prince who joined the Rajputs in 1681 and later fled to Sambhaji was:
new.x: Aurangzeb's son Prince Akbar joined the Rajputs in 1681, fled to Sambhaji and finally to Persia.

new.s: Which Mewar ruler joined Marwar in the Rajput war of 1679–81?
new.x: Rana Raj Singh of Mewar joined Marwar in the war of 1679–81.

new.s: The Jat power built by Churaman after 1700 became which state?
new.x: Churaman built the Jat power that became Bharatpur state.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the revolts under Aurangzeb?
o: Gokula led the Jat revolt of 1669 near Mathura.
The Satnami revolt of 1672 was centred at Narnaul.
The Satnami revolt of 1672 was led by Guru Ghasidas.
Jat leader Rajaram plundered Akbar's tomb at Sikandra.
new.x: Guru Ghasidas belongs to the 19th-century Satnampanth of Chhattisgarh and has no link with the Satnami revolt of 1672.

new.s: Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed by Aurangzeb at Delhi in the year:
new.x: Guru Tegh Bahadur, the 9th Guru, was executed at Delhi in 1675 after refusing to accept Islam.

new.s: The Zafarnama, a Persian letter to Aurangzeb, was written by Guru Gobind Singh after the battle of:
new.x: After Chamkaur (1704) Guru Gobind Singh wrote the Zafarnama accusing Aurangzeb of breaking oaths sworn on the Quran.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Sikh resistance to Aurangzeb:
1. Guru Tegh Bahadur was the 9th Sikh Guru.
2. The Zafarnama was written in Punjabi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Guru Tegh Bahadur was the 9th Guru; the Zafarnama was a Persian letter.

new.s: Who was the last Adil Shahi ruler of Bijapur, defeated by Aurangzeb in 1686?
new.x: Sikandar Adil Shah was presented in silver chains and sent to Daulatabad when Bijapur fell in 1686.

new.s: Which traitor opened the gates of Golconda fort to the Mughals in 1687?
new.x: Abdullah Pani opened the gates; Abdur Razzaq Lari was the loyal defender.

new.s: After the fall of Golconda, Abul Hasan Qutb Shah (Tana Shah) was finally kept at:
new.x: Tana Shah was imprisoned at Bidar, then Daulatabad; Gwalior was where Murad Bakhsh was held.

new.s: Bhakta Ramadasu was the nephew of which Golconda ministers?
new.x: Bhakta Ramadasu was the nephew of Akkanna–Madanna, the ministers murdered in 1686.

new.s: Where was Sambhaji captured before his execution in 1689?
new.x: Sambhaji was captured at Sangameshwar and executed in March 1689.

new.s: Who led the Maratha war against Aurangzeb from 1700 as regent for her infant son Shivaji II?
new.x: Tarabai, Rajaram's widow, led the war from 1700 as regent for Shivaji II.

new.s: From which fort did Rajaram resist the Mughals after becoming Chhatrapati in 1689?
new.x: Rajaram resisted from Jinji and died at Sinhagad in 1700.

new.s: Where did Aurangzeb die in 1707?
new.x: Aurangzeb died at Ahmednagar in 1707 and was buried at Khuldabad.

new.s: Which last Golconda ruler is also buried at Khuldabad, the burial place of Aurangzeb?
new.x: Tana Shah (Abul Hasan Qutb Shah) died in 1699 and was buried at Khuldabad, where Aurangzeb also lies.

new.s: Under the Mansabdari system, mansab ranks ranged from:
new.x: Ranks ran from 10 to 10,000, the highest reserved for princes.

new.s: According to Abul Fazl, how many mansab grades existed in theory?
new.x: Abul Fazl gives 66 grades in theory, of which 33 existed in practice.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about zat and sawar:
1. Zat denoted personal rank, status and salary.
2. The sawar rank could exceed the zat rank.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Zat was the personal rank; under the system the sawar could not exceed the zat.

new.s: Under Shah Jahan's month-scale, a 'sihmaha' jagir yielded:
o: A quarter of its assessed revenue
new.x: Sihmaha meant a quarter-yield; shashmaha meant half-yield.

new.s: State-paid troops placed under mansabdars in the Mughal army were called:
new.x: Dakhili were state-paid troops under mansabdars; tabinan were the mansabdars' own contingents.

new.s: The mansabdars' own contingents in the Mughal army were known as:
new.x: Tabinan were the mansabdars' own contingents; ahadis were the emperor's own troopers.

new.s: In Mughal military administration, 'dagh' referred to:
new.x: Dagh was horse branding; chehra was the descriptive roll and tashiha the muster check.

new.s: The Mughal term 'tashiha' meant:
new.x: Tashiha was the muster check, alongside dagh (branding) and chehra (descriptive roll).

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Mughal muster terms:
1. Chehra was the descriptive roll of soldiers.
2. Akbar revived the dagh and chehra.
3. Walashahi was the emperor's bodyguard.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: All three are correct: chehra was the descriptive roll, Akbar revived dagh and chehra, and walashahi was the bodyguard.

new.s: Which Mughal central official supervised the royal household and the karkhanas?
new.x: The Mir Saman supervised the royal household and karkhanas.

new.s: The Mughal chief justice who administered the Sharia was the:
new.x: The Qazi-ul-Quzat was the chief justice under the Sharia.

new.s: In the Mughal espionage system, the 'waqia-navis' were:
new.x: Waqia-navis were news-writers; khufia-navis wrote secret reports and harkaras were runners/spies.

new.s: In a Mughal sarkar, the official who kept land records and revenue papers was the:
new.x: The Bitikchi kept land records and revenue papers; the Khazanadar was the treasurer.

new.s: Who was the head of the patwaris at the pargana level?
new.x: The Qanungo headed the patwaris and kept records; the Karkun was a clerk.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: The Kotwal handled town police and markets; the Shiqdar was the pargana executive and the Khazanadar the treasurer.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a jagir in the Mughal system?
new.x: Khalisa was crown land, not a jagir; tankhwah, watan and in'am were jagir types.

new.s: A Mughal jagir granted free of any service obligation was called:
new.x: In'am was free of service; tankhwah was in lieu of salary and mashrut was conditional.

new.s: Which historian explained the jagirdari crisis as an agrarian crisis?
new.x: Irfan Habib saw it as an agrarian crisis; Satish Chandra stressed a shortage of jagirs.

new.s: Athar Ali linked the jagirdari crisis mainly to:
o: The influx of Deccani and Maratha nobles
new.x: Athar Ali stressed the influx of Deccani and Maratha nobles under Aurangzeb.

new.s: Under Aurangzeb, a growing number of mansabdars faced a shortage of good land for jagirs, known as:
new.x: More mansabdars and less good land (paibaqi) squeezed the peasants; khalisa was crown land, not jagir land.

new.s: The Mughal city official in charge of police, markets and a watch on newcomers was the:
new.x: The Kotwal was the city police chief who also controlled markets and watched newcomers.

new.s: In Mughal provincial administration, the Diwan-i-Tan dealt with:
new.x: The Diwan-i-Tan handled salaries (tankhwah) and jagir assignments.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: The Muhtasib looked after public morals; the Bakhshi handled military pay and musters.

new.s: In a Mughal sarkar, the Potdar or Khazanadar served as the:
new.x: The Potdar (Khazanadar/Fotadar) was the sarkar treasurer; the Bitikchi was the accountant.

new.s: The Mughal village headman, who also collected revenue, was the:
new.x: The Muqaddam (Patel) was the village headman; the Patwari was the village accountant.

new.s: Who formalised the Dahsala settlement of 1580?
new.x: Raja Todar Mal formalised the zabt system as the Dahsala settlement in 1580.

new.s: Under the Dahsala system, revenue was fixed on the average yield of the past:
new.x: Dahsala rates were based on the average yield of the past ten years, payable in cash.

new.s: Nasaq, an estimate based on past assessments, was used mainly in:
new.x: Nasaq was used in Bengal and Orissa.

new.s: The Mughal revenue system based on sharing of the crop was:
new.x: Batai (ghallabakhshi or bhaoli) shared the crop; kankut estimated the crop.

new.s: In Akbar's land classification, land cultivated every year was called:
new.x: Polaj land was cultivated every year; parauti was left fallow for a short time.

new.s: Land left uncultivated for five years or more was classed as:
new.x: Banjar land lay uncultivated 5 years or more; chachar lay fallow 3–4 years.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Mughal land classes:
1. Chachar land lay fallow for 3–4 years.
2. Parauti paid the polaj rate when cultivated.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: chachar lay fallow 3–4 years, and parauti paid the polaj rate when cultivated.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about jagirdars and zamindars?
o: Jagirdars received revenue in lieu of salary.
Jagirdars held hereditary rights over land.
new.x: Jagirdars' rights were not hereditary; zamindars held hereditary, saleable rights.

new.s: Which historian classified Mughal zamindars as autonomous chiefs, intermediary and primary?
new.x: The three categories of zamindars are S. Nurul Hasan's classification.

new.s: Mughal zamindars who collected revenue from primary zamindars for the state in return for a commission were:
new.x: Intermediary zamindars collected from primary zamindars for the state and got a commission.

new.s: Under Tana Shah, Qutb Shahi Golconda had how many parganas?
new.x: Under Tana Shah Golconda had 37 sarkars and 517 parganas.

new.s: In Qutb Shahi Golconda, the village accountant was called the:
new.x: The kulkarni was the accountant; the mukaddam was the village head and the desai the pargana officer.

new.s: The Chakla, a unit not identical with the sarkar, was prominent in Bengal under:
new.x: The chakla was prominent in Bengal under Murshid Quli Khan.

new.s: How many subas did the Mughal empire have under Aurangzeb?
new.x: Akbar began with 12 and had 15 by the end of his reign; Aurangzeb had 21, Golconda being the 21st.
